transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood), Marcus Patel (Redwood), Diego Alvarez (Redwood), Sofia Marin (ApexOrbit), Tom Okafor (ApexOrbit), Priya Rao (ApexOrbit)

Summary (auto): quick technical preflight ahead of marketplace listing. Discussed packaging options (operator vs container image), VPC/connectivity for Redwood Private, SSO and KMS requirements, E2E telemetry and billing hooks, UAT schedule and deliverables. Agreed on checklist owners and dates.

00:00 - Speaker 1: okay hello everyone, welcome, this is Lara from Redwood, thanks for joining, um this is the preflight for the joint solution accelerator and marketplace listing, we've got maybe 45 minutes, quick agenda: packaging, connectivity, security, telemetry, next steps.
00:25 - Sofia: hi Lara, yep thanks, we have Tom and Priya on the call, I'm Sofia, we'll be owning the listing side from ApexOrbit.
00:45 - Lara: great, Marcus and Diego from our side, Marcus will go over the operator bits and Diego will cover runbooks and telemetry.
01:10 - Marcus: cool, I'll jump in on packaging first. So we recommend two artifacts for a marketplace listing: 1) a deployable operator / helm chart so customers can install on-prem or in VPC, and 2) a containerized image with a quick-start helm values file for cloud marketplace installs. For Azure marketplace you'll want an ARM/uplink manifest; for AWS we've seen installers using the helm chart + an AMI for dedicated.
01:45 - Tom: quick Q — we run a hybrid infra, most customers want a managed listing but with VPC peering to our infra. How do you recommend handling the networking? Do we need to route tokens over a public internet endpoint?
02:12 - Marcus: good question. Redwood offers Private mode where the control plane is customer-managed. For marketplace listing you can offer an on-prem operator that establishes a secure mTLS tunnel back to Redwood, or you can use VPC peering if both sides are in same cloud region. Both patterns avoid public tokens in the clear. There were some folks who, uh, confused mTLS with VPN, so we show both patterns in the checklist.
02:55 - Priya: from security, what's the KMS story? We need to ensure keys never leave our HSM and that logs with PII are redacted. Also need to surface audit logs for compliance.
03:20 - Diego: Redwood integrates with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping, we have server side encryption and also an optional envelope key pattern. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM via S3 or syslog; the Console exposes per-request tracing and token-level cost meta, which you can ship to your logging endpoint. We'll include the exact CloudTrail/Sysdig sample in the packaging doc.
03:58 - Sofia: and regarding pricing metering — customers expect usage-based billing through marketplace. How do we report usage?
04:15 - Lara: marketplace billing is usually handled by the marketplace itself if you list as managed. For dedicated/reserved offers we provide a usage export that can be consumed by your billing system; there's a webhook and CSV export option. We'll include the schema in the checklist.
04:45 - Speaker 2 (Marcus?): I want to show a short slide of the operator deploy pattern — (brief pause) ok so the operator manages model artifacts, KV cache lifecycles, and config maps for quantization profiles. When we install in a private VPC the operator uses a sidecar to manage the KV cache and ephemeral storage.
05:20 - Tom: are there any runtime constraints we should call out? e.g., seq len, model variants, GPU families? our infra has A100 nodes and some customers have older V100s.
05:40 - Marcus: yes, call out supported GPU families and recommended CU counts. For A100 we show throughput numbers at 1k token windows; for V100 we'd recommend smaller batches and the checkpointed model. We'll include fallback model variants for latency vs cost tradeoffs. Also note if you're packaging quantized LLMs we must verify licensing for redistributable artifacts.
06:15 - Priya: licensing is huge, do we need to include model licenses in the listing? Some open models have constraints on commercial redistribution.
06:30 - Diego: yes, our recommended flow is to reference the model and pull from a verified model registry at deploy time, rather than bundling the full weights in the marketplace package. That reduces legal surface and decreases bundle size. We'll add guidance to the checklist about model registry references and a sample values.yaml that points to the model manifest.
07:05 - Sofia: this is helpful. On the publishing timeline, marketplace certification requires a set of docs and an operational runbook — can Redwood help produce the runbook?
07:25 - Lara: absolutely. Diego will lead the runbook and include canary rollouts, rollback steps, and troubleshooting tags for Redwood Console (trace ids, route names). We'll need your input on escalation contacts and SSO endpoints.
07:50 - Tom: about SSO — ApexOrbit is SAML-based for our enterprise customers. Does Redwood support SAML and provisioning mapped roles into the app?
08:05 - Marcus: yes SAML and OIDC are supported, single sign-on mapping to RBAC roles is configurable. For marketplace listings it's good to include a sample SAML metadata file and steps to configure an IdP. We'll add that to the packaging repo.
08:30 - Priya: audit logs — will Redwood keep a tamper-evident audit trail? We may need that for audits.
08:45 - Diego: our audit logging supports immutability patterns via write-once S3 buckets and signed digests if you need that. We'll provide the format and a sample ingestion pipeline to your SIEM.
09:05 - Speaker 3 (Sofia): Great. One worry from our product team is support matrix — who triages customer issues for marketplace deployments? Do we hand off to Redwood support or is it joint?
09:25 - Lara: typical model is joint: Redwood supports runtime/inference and platform issues; ApexOrbit handles customer billing/listing and first-line support for install questions. We can set up an escalation matrix in the runbook and an optional co-managed Slack channel for early pilots.
09:50 - Tom: any specifics on telemetry? we want to show usage per-tenant and per-model variant in our analytics dashboard. What hooks do you expose?
10:12 - Marcus: we expose per-request hooks with tags you can set at deployment or runtime: tenant_id, route, model_variant, campaign_id. Those are available in the Console and also as an export stream via Kinesis or Pub/Sub. There is a lightweight SDK for metrics emission. We'll share sample code.
10:40 - Priya: curious about multi-tenancy isolation in the operator pattern — how do you ensure KV cache isn't cross-tenant?
10:55 - Marcus: operator will provision per-tenant namespaces and enforce ephemeral KV cache isolation using namespace-scoped volumes; we also have config to restrict memory/GPU access per namespace. It's part of the packaging tests in the checklist.
11:20 - Sofia: can we talk about on-prem air-gapped customers? some of ours require no outbound internet at all.
11:35 - Diego: for air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle that includes the control plane with a private registry image and offline install scripts; in those cases model weights are pulled from a vendor-provided storage or shipped on disk and loaded into the registry. We also have an optional offline license server flow. We'll document that in a separate airgap guide.
12:05 - Tom: good. For the marketplace listing metadata, do you have an example of the README and feature list you expect?
12:20 - Lara: yes — short summary, supported deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private/on-prem), certifications (SOC2/ISO/PCI if applicable), required infra, and sample cost/perf numbers. We'll attach a sample listing README in the checklist artifact.
12:45 - Speaker 4 (Marcus): small note on CI — our e2e tests run in both k8s 1.24 and 1.27, we recommend running packaging tests across both. Also include a smoke test that validates SSO and KMS integration.
13:05 - Priya: we'll need the smoke test steps for our security validation team.
13:20 - Diego: sure, I'll include step-by-step: provision staging tenant, run deploy script, validate SSO login, validate key wrap/unbox with provided KMS, run a synthetic inference and check trace id propagation.
13:45 - Sofia: on runbook cadence — what do you see as the go/no-go criteria for listing?
14:00 - Lara: go criteria: successful UAT (staging deploy + smoke tests), security signoff with SOC2 artifacts and KMS proof, packaging lint checks passing, and a runbook with clear rollback steps. No-go would be unresolved data residency or an unsupported model licensing issue.
14:25 - Tom: ok makes sense. We have a question from our legal: how do we represent shared liability in the listing? Are there standard T&Cs Redwood recommends?
14:40 - Lara: we usually provide a template addendum that states run-of-service responsibilities; marketplace agreements vary but we can share a short addendum template for review — legal to legal.
15:00 - Speaker 5 (Sofia): next, UAT dates — we want to aim for mid-December. Is that reasonable?
15:12 - Marcus: yes as long as we get the staging tenant by Dec 10 and the packaging artifacts by Dec 6, we can run UAT the week of Dec 15.
15:30 - Priya: logs retention and redaction — can we set log retention to 90 days and redaction rules for PII?
15:45 - Diego: yes retention window's configurable, redaction rules can be configured at ingestion time. We'll show a sample policy and the exact log redactors we use.
16:10 - Tom: one more on observability — are traces correlated with billing tokens so we can attribute cost per customer?
16:25 - Marcus: yes, we stamp traces with hash of API key/tenant id and include a cost token map in the usage export. That makes it straightforward to attribute cost to tenant or route.
16:45 - Sofia: any blockers you see on your side?
16:55 - Lara: only blocker is finalizing the packaging repo and sample tenant; otherwise sounds straightforward.
17:10 - Tom: do you have sample CI for marketplace certification? like a checklist of required tests?
17:25 - Diego: yes will attach. We'll also include a small script to validate manifest and license headers.
17:40 - Speaker 6 (Priya): ok great, can we recap action items and owners?
17:50 - Lara: sure — high level: Redwood shares packaging checklist and helm/operator examples (Lara/Marcus) by Dec 3-6; Redwood shares runbook and canary rollback (Diego) by Dec 8; ApexOrbit provisions staging tenant and sends SAML metadata + KMS profile (Tom/Priya) by Dec 10; schedule UAT week of Dec 15.
18:25 - Sofia: perfect. We'll follow up with legal for T&C review and schedule a short alignment call with marketing for marketplace listing copy.
18:40 - Lara: thanks everyone. We'll send meeting notes and upload artifacts to the shared drive.
18:50 - Marcus: thanks, bye.
19:00 - Tom: bye.

Artifacts referenced: packaging-checklist.md (link: https://redwood.example/sdks/apexorbit/packaging-checklist), operator-helm-sample (link: https://redwood.example/sdks/apexorbit/helm), runbook-draft (link: https://redwood.example/sdks/apexorbit/runbook-draft).

End of transcript.
